name: Coordination and technical decisions
inputs: Signed work plan and partner role sheets; technical releases from every WP.
work: Savery chairs 36 monthly technical boards and six six-monthly resource reviews, maintains a decision register and resolves interface changes with the affected WP leads. Each partner supplies a named deputy, effort record and quarterly forecast. Scientific changes require a stated test, resource consequence and versioned disposition.
acceptance: Six review records reconcile task, WP and partner totals; no unresolved interface change enters a frozen test; each critical action has an owner and due month.

name: Data quality and reproducibility
inputs: Initial sample and signal schemas from T2.1, T3.1 and T6.1, then measured datasets and executable models.
work: The data officer and the five technical leads implement one sample-to-cartridge-to-run identifier chain, a unit dictionary, access classes, calibration records and model/controller registries. Publish a data management plan by M4 and revise it at M18 and M36. Audit one sample-to-result chain per partner at six reviews, including failed runs and non-public background access.
acceptance: Every released run resolves material batch, forming lot, cartridge, calibration and controller/model versions; raw records remain immutable; all holdout access and deviations are logged.

name: Resources and operational readiness
inputs: Personnel slots, facility calendars and equipment cost bases; workload and risk updates.
work: Partners produce five access and staffing sheets, maintain six rolling FTE and facility-capacity forecasts and check that charged work is unique to this action. The M2 operational review verifies synthesis staff, the kilogram production route, laboratory hosting, pressure-system responsibility and digital access. Reforecast costs at each six-monthly review.
acceptance: All five operating sheets identify accountable staff, equipment owner, eligible charge method and booking capacity; unresolved gaps trigger the risk actions before dependent work starts.

name: Composition exploration and cycle fingerprints
inputs: Nominal heat service and boundary envelope from T6.1; baseline powder and reference structure.
work: IRCELYON researchers explore 12 nominal compositions in two water-stable framework families, using mixed-linker and limited mixed-metal variants where synthesis permits. Savery prepares three genuinely separate 20 g syntheses per composition, giving 36 batches and 0.72 kg. Savery records feed and measured composition, phase identity, activation, yield and solvent use. IRCELYON measures three-temperature isotherms on all 36 batches. UPorto and Savery use the resulting fingerprints to rank operating windows; IKTS checks process compatibility.
acceptance: Downselect four compositions by M9 using a declared score for usable swing, loading-dependent heat, rate and stability; a phase mixture is labelled as such; at least one tunable composition must show a reproducible fingerprint change beyond combined uncertainty, or the claimed composition mechanism is returned for revision.

name: Reproducible production and mechanistic measurements
inputs: T2.1 fingerprints and the early T4.1 transport model; provisional T3.1 forming needs.
work: Savery prepares 12 independent 100 g confirmation batches for four compositions and six 600 g process-development batches for two finalists. A further three 200 g batches support mechanism discrimination. IRCELYON obtains 36 confirmation isotherms, 24 loading-resolved calorimetric profiles and 48 reset-separated dynamic histories covering two chemistries, two thicknesses, two thermal contacts, two preparations and three batch blocks. Use selected diffraction and, only if discriminating, water-sensitive spectroscopy. Calibrate the instrument and vapour path separately. Select one production recipe at M12 from the confirmed finalists so that the 180 kg campaign can run in M13-M23; detailed mechanistic measurements continue to M18. The two-chemistry mechanism blocks use disjoint samples from the existing independently synthesised confirmation/process batches; the three extra 200 g batches supplement targeted observations and are not relabelled as six independent batches.
acceptance: Deliver two traceable powder candidates and uncertainty-qualified constitutive cards by M18; explain composition and scale effects separately; qualify Savery’s single 5 kg line. Record released dry mass per lot, full turnaround including cleaning, and QC rejection before releasing the campaign.

name: Validation batches and ageing
inputs: M12 production recipe decision in T2.2; progressively qualified T3.2 process windows and operating stresses from T6.2.
work: Savery produces 36 independent batches on one 5 kg line of the selected new MOF and allocate six disjoint groups of six batches, three groups to each shaping route. At 85% recovered MOF yield, 153 kg provides 120 kg for validation cartridges, 9 kg for retained characterisation and 24 kg for archive, losses and rework. The planning case assumes 5 kg released dry powder and 32 occupied hours per batch, including cleaning and turnaround. At 180 available line-hours per month in M13–M23, the campaign needs 1,152 of 1,980 hours. At M12 Savery recalculates the batch count from measured output and availability. Baseline powder comprises three independent 60 kg supplier-production batches plus 20 kg development stock. IRCELYON tests 24 material-route-batch-stress coupons for 500 cycles each on a separate ageing apparatus, with pre/post fingerprints and three inspection points. Release independent groups sequentially, with A by M19, B by M21 and C by M23, for final forming and qualification by M24.
acceptance: By M24 all six new-material cartridge groups retain independent batch provenance; within a selected recipe, cycle-working-capacity coefficient of variation is at most 10%, and retained capacity after 500 coupon cycles is at least 90%, or the failure domain and recovery plan are explicitly released. No achieved ageing performance is assumed.

name: Two shaping routes and interface specification
inputs: Reference powder available at M1, the provisional T2.1 fingerprints and T6.1 cartridge envelope.
work: IKTS develops freeze-granulated or gently extruded granules for a permeable bed, and a low-temperature conductive composite or monolithic structure for heat-transfer-limited operation. Use two candidate chemistries, two routes and three process settings per route, with two separately formed 150 g-MOF lots per setting: 24 forming lots consuming 3.6 kg MOF. Measure accessible uptake, binder fraction, dimensions, bulk density, permeability and mechanical integrity. Savery releases an interchangeable thermal and vapour interface at M4. An existing reference-granule process supplies the early rig by M6; this baseline does not wait for experimental route downselection.
acceptance: Two routes have buildable coupons by M10; retain at least 80% of powder working capacity per dry-MOF mass as a target and report capacity per total shaped mass and volume as well; process settings and rejected lots remain traceable.

name: Manufacturing windows and transport parameters
inputs: T3.1 lots, refined powder cards and the independently calibrated T4.1 model.
work: Characterise 24 forming lots and a small set of reference-powder coupons using 12 measurement profiles per lot, giving 288 lot-property profiles. Bound heat conduction, interfacial contact, vapour permeability, effective mass transfer, strength and dimensional spread. UPorto separates intrinsic kinetic parameters from geometry-dependent closures. Downselect one process window for each route using measured useful power and auxiliary-loss estimates rather than surface area alone.
acceptance: M18 process windows state temperature, pressure/shear, binder, yield and tolerances; the model can use their parameters with uncertainty; reject a window that only raises peak uptake while losing service feasibility or increasing net resource use.

name: Independent cartridges and quality release
inputs: T2.3 batch groups, T3.2 windows and the fixed T6.1 interface.
work: Manufacture twelve complete two-bed cartridge sets: two chemistries times two routes times three independent assembly blocks. Each set contains 20 kg active dry MOF across two 10 kg beds. A set is a matched pair of replaceable bed internals, not a second machine. Qualify mass, dimensions, thermal contact, conductance, attrition and leak-compatible assembly. Savery provides the one reusable 10 kW mechanical module, pressure housing and metering; IKTS supplies the shaped internals and production travellers.
acceptance: Release all twelve sets and as-built cards by M24, with M25 reserved for correction; do not mix validation-group powder with development material; the first cartridge per route meets the agreed interface and metering conditions before the remaining lots are built.

name: Conservation models and identifiable experiments
inputs: Reference MOF data and early bench topology, then measured T2.1 and T3.1 cards.
work: UPorto starts a distributed heat-and-mass balance model on the reference material at M1. Compare equilibrium/transport, water-population and additional internal-state descriptions with common observation mappings and physically bounded parameters. Design the 48 mechanism histories to separate thermal-contact, thickness and preparation effects. HPE receives a runnable reference simulator and common state/action/observation schema by M4; Savery qualifies actual actuator and sensor dynamics.
acceptance: M10 model release closes mass and energy numerically, preserves non-negative dissipation in its stated domain and documents which parameters the available observations can identify; model complexity increases only when withheld whole histories discriminate it.

name: Reduced models and state estimation
inputs: T4.1 candidate models, T2.2 dynamic records and T6.2 interventions; T3.2 transport maps.
work: Build a control model with a declared minimum sufficient state, an estimator and predictive intervals for each physical configuration. Test at least three estimator structures and three model orders using whole-run partitions. Predict heat, water inventory and internal temperatures under held-out preparation and boundary blocks. HPE checks computational cost and deployability; material and shaping leads test the interpretation of inferred states.
acceptance: By M22 the selected ROM and estimator meet a five-second supervisory step with 99th-percentile solve time below one second on declared hardware; on development holdouts, heat prediction NRMSE is at most 10% of rated duty, inventory error is at most 5% of measured swing, and 90% predictive intervals have stated empirical coverage. Failure narrows the earned domain rather than hiding extrapolation.

name: Prospective prediction and model correction
inputs: M22 models, M24 frozen policies and the sealed T6.3 validation manifest.
work: Freeze model form, fitting rules and observation mappings before the four final challenge histories are released. Use independently designated calibration specimens, while reserving batch group C, the four boundary histories and their terminal states from fitting. Compare complete-trajectory errors and cycle totals. Diagnose failures during M31-M34 with a versioned correction branch; original prospective results remain unchanged and correction claims use the reserved rerun histories.
acceptance: Deliver M34 predictive-transfer evidence with separate results for cross-batch, cross-history and cross-boundary tests; any adapted parameter is labelled as calibrated, and no validation set is silently reused as training.

name: Control baselines and common information
inputs: Reference simulator at M4, T6.1 actuator limits and a shared training-data manifest.
work: HPE implements an optimised fixed-cycle policy and economic MPC before new MOFs arrive. Both can use the same sensors, state estimator, permitted actuator range and declared boundary forecasts later available to RL. Fix an economic objective using measured drive heat, all electrical work and qualified heat delivery, with a common unmet-service penalty. Each strategy receives six full development histories per physical configuration and a declared, comparable tuning-compute allowance.
acceptance: M12 baseline release includes tuned fixed-cycle schedules, an MPC implementation, objective and forecast contracts, and reproducible tuning logs; the fixed baseline may optimise offline but cannot access final challenge histories.

name: Constrained RL for energy flow allocation
inputs: T5.1 baseline, T4.2 ROM/estimator and measured process and actuator uncertainties.
work: Train a constrained RL policy to allocate source heat, regeneration timing, heat recovery, vapour circulation and branch pressure assistance. Use twenty training seeds and up to one thousand simulated episodes per seed for each of four physical configurations, within 1,500 CPU-hours of the 5,000 CPU-hour control allocation and a separately costed 1,000 GPU-hours. A model-based safety filter enforces temperature, pressure, flow and service constraints; a watchdog returns to the qualified fixed policy. Test 36 normal/fault histories for each of three policies in HIL, giving 108 tests.
acceptance: M24 deployment candidate has zero unresolved hard-limit violations in HIL, deterministic fallback, complete logs and bounded real-time inference. RL has an explicit scientific test against MPC; deployment is conditional on safety qualification, not on presuming a savings gain.

name: Closed loop comparison and transfer
inputs: Qualified policies from T5.2 and the physical T6.3 protocol; identical allowed measurements and forecasts.
work: Deploy all three policies on the four physical configurations. Freeze tuning at M24 and run the 144 final whole-history tests with blocked order across independent assembly groups. Compare economic cost, electrical and thermal inputs, delivered-service error and feasibility. Evaluate RL-minus-MPC interaction with material and shape; use eight reserved transfer runs at an adjacent hot-water setpoint only after the primary dataset is complete.
acceptance: Report effect sizes and uncertainty by independent batch/assembly block. Retain MPC as the deployment recommendation if RL is equivalent, less robust or more resource-intensive; the tested RL mechanism and its domain remain substantive scientific outputs.

name: Early instrumented reference platform
inputs: Existing reference MOF and published thermophysical relations; the primary 10 kW hot-water service.
work: Savery engineers build one reconfigurable 10 kW two-bed laboratory module with two 10 kg-MOF bed internals, measured source, rejection and useful-heat circuits, a calibrated vapour path, a bypassable vapour mover and branch compressor. Commission on reference granules by M8 using 160 rig-hours. The M4 topology and instrument release lets modelling and control proceed in parallel. Meter all heat inputs and outputs, each electrical feeder, liquid-water inventories, pressure, temperatures and commanded/realised actuation.
acceptance: At M8, calibrations and blank/reference tests target cycle energy residual within 5% of accounted input, mass residual within 2% of transferred water and 95% expanded useful-heat uncertainty at most 5%; unresolved residuals suspend gain claims and trigger re-instrumentation.

name: Actuator ablation and component iterations
inputs: T6.1 qualified rig; development cartridges and progressively updated models/policies.
work: Run 32 complete four-hour ablation histories across passive, circulation-only, compression-only and combined modes to separate transport and pressure effects. Allocate 120 further rig-hours to repeated reference checks and 72 four-hour controller-development histories across four physical configurations and three policies. Complete two component-iteration cycles by M16 and M22, correcting metering, heat leaks, contact or conductance before validation hardware is frozen.
acceptance: M22 readiness pack identifies useful service, feasible actuator domain, parasitic-loss floor and a measured reference baseline. If active assistance loses its net benefit, preserve bypass comparisons and test the resulting feasibility domain without a fabricated energy-saving percentage.

name: Blinded integrated comparison
inputs: T3.3 independent cartridge sets; frozen models, estimator and policies; M24 validation manifest.
work: Use four physical cells (reference/new MOF times granule/conductive structure), three policies, four unseen complete boundary/history challenges and three independent assembly blocks: 144 eight-hour runs, including four hours service, two hours reset and two hours setup/stabilisation. Schedule first comparisons in M25-M32. Reserve twenty-four additional eight-hour histories for faults, declared model correction and replication in M33-M34. Verify service equality, inventory closure and full reset before any paired saving calculation.
acceptance: Primary evidence reports service feasibility and the complete thermal/electrical boundary for all cells. At nominal 55 C source, 25 C rejection and 70 C hot-water delivery, test the 10 kW design point; if a cell cannot meet it, report its feasible duty and restrict matched-input comparisons to a predeclared common duty, down to 5 kW, with capacity differences reported separately.

name: Evidence consolidation and TRL 4 assessment
inputs: All prospective results, failure/correction logs and manufacturing records.
work: Complete eight eight-hour transfer histories at an adjacent delivery temperature, retain three independent nominal replications per physical cell from the primary dataset, and reconcile every reported KPI to raw signals. Produce a laboratory TRL 4 evidence file for the material-component-control chain, including the qualified operating domain, independent repeatability, uncertainty, reproducible analysis and remaining scale-up limitations. No site demonstrator is built.
acceptance: At M36, technical leads can reproduce the principal comparisons from released data and code; evidence supports validation in a laboratory only, and failed configurations or claims remain visible.

name: Early dissemination exploitation and communication plan
inputs: Scientific objectives, background inventory and partner exploitation interests.
work: Savery prepares a distinct plan by M6 with four result families, target users, ownership interfaces, publication review and a communication calendar. Materials, manufacturing, modelling/control and system evidence each receive a named exploitation owner. Define six research-output submissions, three public technical events and six bounded adopter requirements interviews over the action, subject to normal later activity approvals.
acceptance: M6 plan is separate from the M4 data management plan, identifies audiences and actions, and protects unpublished recipes, patent matter and commercial background.

name: Manufacturing sustainability and economic boundaries
inputs: Measured batch yields, solvent/material inputs, process windows and integrated energy balances.
work: IRCELYON and IKTS supply production and forming inventories; UPorto and Savery assess four physical configurations per qualified kWh of delivered heat and per reusable cartridge. Quantify material demand, solvent use, yield, cycling life and full thermal/electrical inputs. Compare current laboratory manufacture and two explicitly projected production scales without claiming industrial performance or an ISO-certified lifecycle assessment.
acceptance: M32 assessment gives functional unit, allocation, data quality, electricity/source-heat assumptions and sensitivity to life and yield; a net-benefit claim excludes neither regeneration/reset nor auxiliaries.

name: Protected results and subsequent development
inputs: T7.1 plan, technical releases, measured validation and partner background declarations.
work: Update exploitation and communication at M18 and M36. Hold three technical exchange events, prepare six research-output submissions, complete six adopter requirement interviews and maintain four exploitable-result records. Savery leads the subsequent whole heat-recovery equipment/system route; IKTS supports manufacturing transfer, while UPorto and HPE define model/control reuse. Each partner reviews access rights before disclosure; neither patents nor downstream commercial performance are presumed.
acceptance: M36 route assigns result owner, access terms, next evidence and resources needed beyond TRL 4. Scientific and exploitation claims remain bounded by measured results; no additional beneficiary or site demonstrator is implied.
